title: ee.daemon.request.v1
description: Length-prefixed JSON request envelope for the optional `ee daemon` Unix-domain socket RPC introduced by bd-oja31 (SRR1 hot-mode skeleton). Wire framing: 4-byte big-endian unsigned length, then exactly that many bytes of UTF-8 JSON conforming to this schema. The daemon process binds the socket at `${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR}/ee/daemon.sock` on Linux when the runtime dir is a private per-user directory, and at the per-UID `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ee-${uid}/daemon.sock` fallback on macOS or wherever XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is unset, empty, or a shared temp root (XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is not standard on Darwin); the daemon never defaults to a bare shared socket name directly under /tmp (bd-3j0td, bd-10ex7). The daemon is opt-in; every CLI command continues to work when the socket is absent. The v1 schema covers `ee.daemon.capabilities` (schema/method discovery), `ee.daemon.echo` (round-trip integrity check), and `ee.daemon.context` (workspace-bound canonical `ee pack` execution that returns an `ee.response.v2` object in the daemon result). Requests carry `agent_id` and optional `workspace_id` so warm-load, audit, and authorization logic can attribute calls without changing the v1 envelope. Workspace-bound methods such as `ee.daemon.context` require a non-empty `workspace_id` matching the daemon's bound workspace and return `daemon_method_unauthorized` on absence or mismatch. This v1 envelope is strict by design: unknown top-level fields and unknown methods are rejected. Clients that might speak a newer protocol MUST first call `ee.daemon.capabilities` with `ee.daemon.request.v1`, inspect the advertised request/response schema versions, method names, and authorization map, then downgrade or fall back to the in-process CLI path when the needed contract is absent.

request_id.description: Caller-chosen identifier echoed in the matching response. Recommended shape: ULID or UUIDv7. The daemon does not assign request ids; missing or non-matching ids in responses indicate a framing bug or a redirected connection.

agent_id.description: Caller-chosen local agent identity echoed in the matching response. This is an attribution/audit field reserved by bd-1clej; daemon authorization uses peer UID plus method/workspace policy and MUST NOT be inferred from agent_id alone.

workspace_id.description: Optional caller workspace identity echoed in the matching response when present. Required for registered workspace-bound methods such as `ee.daemon.context`; those methods return `daemon_method_unauthorized` when this value is absent, blank, or does not match the daemon's bound workspace.

method.description: Method dispatch name. `ee.daemon.capabilities` returns the daemon protocol discovery payload for v1-to-v2 negotiation. `ee.daemon.echo` returns the supplied params in redaction-stable form for round-trip integrity checks when explicitly enabled. `ee.daemon.context` is a same-UID, workspace-bound canonical `ee pack` path; it requires `workspace_id` authorization first, validates method params, and returns a daemon result containing the canonical `ee.response.v2` pack envelope.

params.description: Method-specific parameters. For `ee.daemon.capabilities`, callers SHOULD send an empty object and the daemon ignores its contents. For `ee.daemon.echo` this is an arbitrary JSON object that will be returned in redaction-stable form when echo is explicitly enabled. For `ee.daemon.context`, send a compact pack request object: `task` or `query` (required), `workspacePath` / `workspace_path` / `workspace` (required), optional `databasePath`, `indexDir`, `maxTokens`, `candidatePool`, `maxResults`, `profile`, `speed`, `sourceMode`, `strictSourceMode`, `packProfile`, `resourceProfile`, output-pruning booleans, `readOnly`, `explain`, `noPackDna`, and `timeoutMs`. Authorization uses the envelope `workspace_id`; pack semantics use the canonical in-process pack path.
